candidate.derivedAnswer: D: Rotating a rectangle through one full revolution about one of its sides
candidate.answerReason: In Figure 4, the rotation axis lies along a side of the rectangle. Perpendicular segments across the rectangle sweep equal-radius disks along the axis, forming a cylinder. Figures 1 and 2 instead describe a cone and a sphere.

methods.label: Recognizing solids formed by rotation
methods.explanation: Rotating a rectangle about one side produces a cylinder. Rotating a right triangle produces a cone, and rotating a semicircle produces a sphere.
methods.levelReason: Recognizing the solid swept out by a plane region requires only elementary spatial visualization.
